title: PowerPoint on the web: Copilot Agent Mode can reference SharePoint and OneDrive files named in a prompt
summary: The feature description, rollout facts and documented controls are supported. Add the source for presentation creation in a new file, and narrow the OneDrive checklist instruction to the control actually shown in the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap products are PowerPoint and Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["PowerPoint", "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.where: front matter: status; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The feature is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: title; front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: This roadmap item covers the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap calls the capability Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users can mention a SharePoint or OneDrive file by name in a PowerPoint Copilot prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: Copilot can use the mentioned file as context to create the presentation.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.claim: Implicit file references previously were not supported for files in these locations.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.claim: Users need not manually attach or upload the file first.
claims.quote: This update makes it easier to use relevant Microsoft 365 content without manually attaching or uploading the file.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft associates this feature with roadmap ids 555894, 555895 and 555897.
claims.quote:
Roadmap ID:
- [555894](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?filters=&searchterms=555894)
- [555895](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?filters=&searchterms=555895)
- [555897](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/roadmap?filters=&searchterms=555897)

claims.claim: Roadmap item 555895 is the Desktop entry for this feature.
claims.quote: Record 555895: "platforms": ["Desktop"]; "description": "You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint."

claims.claim: Roadmap item 555897 is the Mac entry for this feature.
claims.quote: Record 555897: "platforms": ["Mac"]; "description": "You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint."

claims.claim: The release note lists Windows, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: Reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows, Mac, Web]

claims.claim: The feature entry appears under updates released between September 22, 2026, and October 06, 2026.
claims.quote:
October 06, 2026
Updates released between September 22, 2026, and October 06, 2026.

claims.claim: Copilot features roll out gradually to a subset of tenant users before expanding.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot references files within the signed-in user's existing access rather than granting new permissions.
claims.quote: Permissions come first. Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can surface already overshared content to people who have access.
claims.quote: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions. If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: a user invokes it by naming a file while creating a presentation.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document. Ask Copilot to create a presentation using information from that file.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No feature-specific file-reference switch is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference files administration controls; PowerPoint implicit file references admin switch Graph PowerShell. Opened release-notes and copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center; neither documents this switch.

claims.claim: The generated presentation is a new file built from referenced content.
claims.quote: Now, when creating a presentation using Copilot from an existing presentation, it creates the new presentation in a new file without affecting the original presentation.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/previous-year-release-notes#september-30,-2025 to sources for the new-file statement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint supports sensitivity-label inheritance for newly created content.
claims.quote: Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.

claims.claim: The inherited source label includes its protection settings.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited, with the label's protection settings.

claims.claim: When multiple files are used, the highest-priority sensitivity label is inherited.
claims.quote: If multiple files are used to create new content, the sensitivity label with the highest priority is used for label inheritance.

claims.claim: Label inheritance is not supported for content encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Label inheritance isn't supported for content encrypted with user-defined permissions.

claims.claim: Copilot uses the same underlying data-access controls as other Microsoft 365 services.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: The release note does not identify which component fetches the referenced file.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint SharePoint OneDrive reference file retrieval component. Opened the complete file-reference entry in Microsoft 365 Copilot release-notes; it describes prompting and context, not a fetching component.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[2].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A sensitivity-label condition in a DLP policy for the Copilot location can exclude labelled items from processing.
claims.quote: To set this up, create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Excluded labelled items can remain in citations without their content being used in the response.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: The release-note entry describes no background, scheduled or source-file write action.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint implicit references background scheduled source files. Opened the complete file-reference entry in Microsoft 365 Copilot release-notes; its steps describe a user prompt and presentation creation, not these actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: DLP policy changes can take up to four hours to reach Copilot.
claims.quote: Updates to a DLP policy can take up to four hours to reflect in the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork experiences.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes require propagation time.
claims.quote: Because the setting must propagate across indexing systems, updates can take time to become fully effective.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap and release-note entry do not name a licence tier for implicit file references.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint SharePoint OneDrive file references licensing Copilot. Read roadmap 555894, the complete release-notes entry and copilot-overview; the item and entry name no licence tier for implicit references.

claims.claim: The roadmap and release-note entry name no feature-specific meter or charge.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint SharePoint OneDrive file references licensing Copilot. Read roadmap 555894, its release-notes entry and copilot-overview including usage-based billing; the item and entry state no meter or charge for this feature.

claims.claim: The Copilot overview describes the add-on licence as providing the full Copilot experience in PowerPoint and the other named Office apps.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users can use Copilot in PowerPoint without the add-on.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) does not give the same Copilot-in-PowerPoint entitlement as Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic).
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Some Basic Copilot features are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). It doesn't include full chat integration. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: The mixed model describes the documented Basic and add-on product tiers, while qualifying the entitlement to this particular feature as unresolved.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience (some features are subject to fair use limits), which includes everything in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic)

claims.claim: Learn documents Basic and Premium experiences that include Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) license and experience
Microsoft 365 apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote)
Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license and experience
Microsoft 365 apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote)

claims.claim: The cited sources do not establish whether removing the add-on removes this particular implicit-reference capability.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint SharePoint OneDrive file references licensing Copilot; PowerPoint implicit file references admin switch Graph PowerShell. Read release-notes and copilot-overview: general tiers are described, but this feature's tier is not identified.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP page refers licensing questions to Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans and Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions.
claims.quote:
Licensing
For information on licensing, see
- Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans
- Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is supported for SharePoint sites, not OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change existing access permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly classify a file named in a PowerPoint prompt as covered or exempt from Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Searched: Restricted Content Discovery PowerPoint file mentioned prompt. Read sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery and the file-reference release-notes entry; they distinguish discovery and content already in use, but do not classify this prompt case.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: User licences are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense adds or removes user licences.
claims.quote:
Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to.
POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request body's removeLicenses collection identifies licences to remove.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: The stated Purview route through Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations selects the Copilot policy location.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule call is the reference's Copilot rule example for blocking processing.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The example creates the Copilot policy first using New-DlpCompliancePolicy with EnforcementPlanes set to CopilotExperiences.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use by the user.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label exclusion is available in Copilot in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
claims.quote:
Block files and emails with sensitivity labels from being processed
This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: The sensitivity-label rule supports stored files and actively open files.
claims.quote:
A rule configured to protect items with sensitivity labels applies to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork and supports the following content:
- File items, which are stored and items that are actively open.

claims.claim: Word, Excel and PowerPoint evaluate this Copilot DLP policy at file open.
claims.quote: In Word, Excel, and PowerPoint the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy to prevent Copilot from processing content is evaluated at file open.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label applied mid-session affects DLP enforcement the next time the file is opened.
claims.quote: If a sensitivity label is applied mid-session, the policy will be enforced starting the next time the file is opened.

claims.claim: DLP policy simulation mode is available for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Policy simulation mode is available for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells readers to rely on is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Plan separately for OneDrive: Restricted Content Discovery is not supported for OneDrive sites, so rely on permissions and DLP there. The table contains licence assignment, Restricted Content Discovery and DLP rows, but no permissions row.
claims.fix: Replace the OneDrive checklist bullet with: 'Plan separately for OneDrive: Restricted Content Discovery is not supported for OneDrive sites; check the DLP policy described in the controls table.'
